newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya defies U.N. with pilgrim flight to Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Libya defies U.N. with pilgrim flight to Saudi.

text.p: A Libyan Arab Airlines plane has landed at Jeddah airport carrying Moslem pilgrims to Saudi Arabia in defiance of United Nations sanctions.
The official Libyan news agency JANA said on Saturday the flight was the first of other departures planned from several Libyan airports to carry haj pilgrims.
The agency, monitored in Tunis, did not say when the aircraft landed.

Unauthorised flights to and from Libya are banned under U.N. sanctions imposed on Tripoli for its refusal to hand over for trial two suspects wanted in connection with the bombing of a U.S. airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988.
On March 20, a U.N. sanctions committee said it had given permission for an Egyptian airline, EgyptAir, to make 45 return flights between Libya and Jeddah with Libyans making the annual pilgrimage.

The committee approved similar a arrangement last year. Last year also and the year before, Libya symbolically sent a Libyan plane with pilgrims, but the rest of the pilgrims' flights were provided by Egyptair under U.N. approval.
